text:
Seth Jarvis spent last spring lifting the Stanley Cup with Carolina, and this fall coming back from shoulder surgery. Cory Lavalette of the North State Journal wrote this week that Jarvis "looks like his normal, elite self." Seven games in, our numbers mostly agree, with one asterisk.

The points are there: one goal and six assists, and the Hurricanes control 62% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he's on at five-on-five. That's a winger whose line is driving play, not one hanging on.

The asterisk is his own shot. He's generating about 1.0 expected goals per 60 minutes, down from 1.38 last season, when he scored 32. Only 13 shots on goal in seven games, and two games with none. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the best at getting to the home-plate area last year (86th percentile), so watch whether that returns as the shoulder settles. Our range for his season still runs 17 to 32 goals. We'd lean toward the top half once the shots start coming.
headline: Jarvis is back, and the chances say so
